console.label: Console
console.summary: The React browser application: five workspaces — overview, field, history, decisions, money. It reads the same JSON showcase Jarvis reads and computes nothing of its own.

jarvis.label: Jarvis
jarvis.summary: The console's visual assistant: a question in natural language turns into a scene of cards built from the same JSON showcase. Orchestrator, tools, knowledge base, number guard and sessions live in application/jarvis.

web.label: Static server and proxy
web.summary: Port 8000: serves the built frontend and the JSON showcase, and forwards everything under the /api/jarvis/ prefix to the Jarvis service, so the browser always talks to a single origin.

jarvis-service.label: Jarvis service (8010)
jarvis-service.summary: A separate process and a separate compose service on port 8010, on the stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer. The response is a chunked text/event-stream with a keep-alive comment every 15 seconds so idle proxies do not drop a slow answer.

llm.label: Model client
llm.summary: Chat providers: OpenRouter primary, Anthropic fallback. The orchestrator receives a ChatClient from the outside and knows nothing of urllib or http. Without a key the service still starts and answers 503, naming the variable to set.

search.label: Schedule search
search.summary: Optimisation: it picks a setpoint schedule for the whole control horizon, leaning on the fast model instead of the hydrodynamic simulator. The search strategy and the seed are recorded in the run manifest.

surrogate.label: Fast reservoir model
surrogate.summary: A trained reservoir response model with an NPV head and an out-of-distribution detector: it answers in seconds where the simulator needs hours. Its versions and the NPV head version are pinned in the run provenance.

policy.label: Agent hierarchy
policy.summary: Three decision levels: the field coordinator hands injection quotas to areas, the group allocator splits a quota between wells, and the well executor applies rules R0 to R7. Every decision lands in the journal.

physics.label: Physical invariants
physics.summary: Seven checks of the response: non-negativity, water-cut range, monotonic cumulatives, no flow from a shut well, bottomhole pressure limit, injection response and material balance. A skipped invariant counts as a failed invariant.

economics.label: Economics and NPV
economics.summary: It computes the net present value by the organisers' methodology from the normatives instead of storing it next to the schedule. Derived quantities — NPV, event cost, ESP size — are always computed.

opm.label: OPM Flow
opm.summary: The real hydrodynamic simulator in a container with a pinned image digest: it is the arbiter. A fast-model prediction becomes a result only after OPM has run on the same schedule.

deck.label: The Model_Z deck
deck.summary: The organisers' reservoir model: grid geometry and its properties — porosity, net-to-gross, permeabilities, cell activity, zones and equilibrium regions. Everything drawn on the reservoir maps comes from the deck.

cases.label: Cases and constraints
cases.summary: The competition constraints and the cases derived from them: injection and liquid limits, production floors, well outages, infrastructure bottomhole pressure limits and the compensation corridor. Every value carries its source.

runs.label: Runs
runs.summary: Every run is isolated in its own directory: a manifest with the status and the schedule hash, the schedule itself, the prediction, the OPM work directory, the validation and the economics. Only the submit step writes the ready_to_submit status.

submission.label: Submission package
submission.summary: The claimed NPV together with hashes: of the canonical schedule, the package content, the deck, the economics configuration, the methodology and the constraints, plus the OPM image and the commit. The status promises a package that exists.

webdata.label: JSON showcase
webdata.summary: The export of results into static JSON: the per-step timeline, the NPV breakdown, the connectivity graph, the decision hierarchy, the rule journal and the rule contributions. The console and Jarvis read this, not a database.

knowledge.label: Knowledge base
knowledge.summary: The curated files: a glossary of domain terms with formulas, units and sources, and a guide to the screens with their controls and spotlight anchors. Jarvis explains terms and screens only from here.

docs.label: Project documents
docs.summary: The task statement, the architecture, the plans, the jury answers and the write-ups. They are indexed by a BM25 full-text search over sections so Jarvis quotes a document instead of retelling it from memory.

console->web.label: static files and the JSON showcase

console->jarvis.label: the question and the screen context

jarvis->llm.label: a request carrying the tool descriptions

search->policy.label: setpoints from rules R0 to R7

surrogate->physics.label: the response fed to the seven invariants

search->runs.label: schedule and prediction into the run directory

runs->opm.label: the same schedule sent for verification

opm->runs.label: the verified NPV and the violations

opm->economics.label: the simulator response for the methodology

runs->submission.label: the submission package with its hashes

policy->webdata.label: the hierarchy and the decision journal
